RYA: A Scandinavian knotted-pile woollen rug, used as bed-cover and tapestry.
RYANS: A locality in the Shire of East Gippsland, eastern Victoria, Australia.
RYBINSK: A city in Yaroslavl Oblast, Russia.
RYDE: A town and civil parish with a town council on the northeast coast of the Isle of Wight, England.
RYDER: A gold coin of Zealand (Netherlands) worth 14 florins.
RYE: A grain used extensively in Europe for making bread, beer, and (now generally) for animal fodder.
RYEBREAD: A bread made partly or entirely with rye flour, which may be wholemeal (wholegrain) flour or not.
RYEFLOUR: Flour that has been made or prepared from rye.
RYEGRASS: Any of several species of tufted grasses of the genus Lolium.
RYELAND: A sheep breed originating in England.
RYES: A commune in Calvados department, Normandy, France.
RYESEED: Caraway seed, used whole as a flavoring in the best-known type of rye bread, and often mistakenly assumed to be the rye
RYO: A gold currency unit in the shakkanhō system in pre-Meiji Japan.
RYU: A Japanese school of a specific discipline, usually martial arts.
RYUKYU: A chain of islands in Japan roughly between Kyushu and Taiwan.
RYUKYUAN: Of, relating to, or derived from Ryukyu.
